facts.text: Off-road validation should structure the test space in three layers rather than one Cartesian matrix: an operating-domain taxonomy, a scenario catalog, and parameterised scenario families.

facts.text: Parameterised scenario families at functional, logical and concrete levels, with a probability distribution over their parameters, feed sampling, search and estimation.

facts.text: ISO 21815 and the EMESRT PR-5A storyboards are off-road anchors for structuring the validation test space.

facts.text: ISO 34501 to ISO 34505 and ASAM OpenODD are on-road templates whose structure transfers to off-road validation but whose content does not.

facts.text: No single test-selection method serves every validation job.

facts.text: Combinatorial t-way designs guarantee discrete test coverage.

facts.text: Space-filling designs cover continuous parameters and train surrogate models.

facts.text: Falsification and adaptive search are test-selection methods for finding failures.

facts.text: Importance sampling estimates small probabilities only when the field distribution is known.

facts.text: A frozen stratified random sample is the only basis for a release rate claim.

facts.text: With zero misses allowed, demonstrating a miss rate of at most 1% at 95% one-sided confidence requires 299 independent trials per claimed population.

facts.text: With zero misses allowed, demonstrating a miss rate of at most 0.1% at 95% one-sided confidence requires 2,995 independent trials per claimed population.

facts.quote: at most 0.01% needs 29,956.

facts.text: With zero misses allowed, demonstrating miss rates of at most 1%, 0.1% and 0.01% at 99% confidence requires respectively 459, 4,603 and 46,050 independent trials per claimed population.
facts.quote: At 99% confidence the figures are 459, 4,603 and 46,050.

facts.text: A 1% miss-rate claim in each of 20 critical strata at 95% one-sided confidence requires about 6,000 zero-miss trials; this volume is feasible only in simulation or hardware-in-the-loop.

facts.text: Statistical trial requirements are the binding constraint on demonstrating validation performance.
facts.quote: The statistics are the binding constraint.

facts.text: False-alarm validation needs exposure hours rather than staged targets.
facts.quote: False alarms need exposure hours, not staged targets.

facts.text: With zero events in T representative operating hours, the 95% upper bound on the event rate is approximately 3/T, or exactly 2.996/T, under Poisson mathematics.

facts.text: Under the zero-event Poisson calculation, 300 representative operating hours with no unnecessary brake supports a 95% upper-bound claim of fewer than one unnecessary brake per 100 hours.

facts.text: Clustered alarms, such as alarms on every bucket pass or every dust cloud, violate the Poisson assumption and need block or overdispersed models.

facts.text: Field exposure alone cannot demonstrate rare-event performance.

facts.text: Validation governance should keep discovery campaigns, estimation campaigns, and deterministic requirement and regression campaigns separate.

facts.text: Deterministic requirement and regression tests answer whether a change has broken a required behaviour.

facts.text: Collision-mitigation tuning should be a constrained multi-objective problem: make missed or late interventions a hard constraint, then optimise false warnings, unnecessary brakes and productivity loss.
